condition: Every expectation derives from the SPEC's text, never from dev's plan or code; each carries the line that determines it. Where the spec does not determine a value it is marked OPEN and asked, never guessed.
derivation_note: The 972 cells are GENERATED from the ordered predicate and the candidate set above, not transcribed. A hand table over this product would be 972 rows nobody could check; a generated one cannot disagree with the predicate it came from. Regenerate rather than edit. Amendment 2 did not REPLACE the v10 expectations: the v11 predicate was first re-evaluated against all 486 frozen cells at record_kind=procedural and had to reproduce every one of them exactly before the declarative half was generated (the check is in the amendment's generator and fails hard). So the 486 are evidence, not assumption.

named_cells.accounting_above_the_cap: on a store with more describable records than `limit`: len(descriptions) == min(total_describable, limit) AND total_describable + len(withheld) == the visible population

declarative_bytes_unchanged.expect: BYTE-IDENTICAL — today's 8 keys with the three deliberate nulls (`derived_from`, `source_id`, `origin`) present; `record_kind` ABSENT, not null
declarative_bytes_unchanged.setup: serialize a declarative record's `Provenance` on the pre-feature oracle and on the feature build
declarative_bytes_unchanged.why_it_matters: research's pre-seal pass on v11's first draft found this asserted with no mechanism; the fix is a wrap-mode model_serializer that pops the key when None (executed, §2c-ii). The mutant is the DEFAULT serializer, which emits `"record_kind":null` on every record and changes the bytes of every existing row and every 0029 journal `state` payload. Two oracles must catch it independently.

declarative_control.derives_from: §4a-ii (v11): the candidate set is re-based on the STAMP — a declarative-stamped record without a basis is never a candidate
declarative_control.expect: in NEITHER list, and NOT counted toward total_describable + len(withheld)
declarative_control.setup: declarative-stamped records present in the same store, BOTH with a registered relation and with an unregistered one
declarative_control.why_it_matters: the accounting identity alone would not catch a declarative record leaking into the population; without this control, 'the visible population' is unfalsifiable. v11 adds the second half: the unregistered variant is what makes V-KIND-STAMPED's central claim falsifiable — a registry change must move NO declarative record's treatment.

named_cells.existence_oracle: an unauthorised principal's DescribeResult for an existing HIDDEN record must be byte-identical to the result for a nonexistent record

cells.case: both stripped, relation registered PROCEDURAL by the importing host
cells.why_it_matters: the cell the whole finding is about: removing both markers must not move the decision in the permissive direction. It is also V-IMPORT-…'s mutant — drop the registry signal and ONLY this cell fails

the counterweight, and the one research would have got wrong: nothing readable says procedural, so it IS a declarative record under an out-of-vocabulary relation. Refusing here would invent a signal that is not there, and would break every legacy custom relation

cells.case: foreign "procedural" stamp, relation registered DECLARATIVE by this host
cells.why_it_matters: the importing host's registry does not get to launder a foreign stamp away; the stamp is an independent signal and fires first

cells.case: file stamped FORMAT 10 carrying either key
cells.why_it_matters: I10 strips the keys, so signals 1 and 2 cannot fire — signal 3 is the only one left, which is why three signals are needed and not two

import_three_signal_refusal.derives_from: v12 §2 (import row), §2c default-path row, §4e, V-IMPORT-REFUSES-PROCEDURAL-UNLESS-RESTORE; external round 3 F2
import_three_signal_refusal.rule: On the DEFAULT import path a record is refused as procedural (`procedural_import_refused`) if ANY of three independent signals fires, and the refusal NAMES which — first in the order stamp, basis, registry. Never a bare refusal.

kind_conflict_counted.derives_from: §4a-ii conjunct 1 (v11, round-2 F2); V-KIND-STAMPED's third mutant
kind_conflict_counted.setup: a record whose stamp says declarative and whose basis is not None (DB-level tamper; no shipped writer produces it)
kind_conflict_counted.why_it_matters: procedural BY FLOOR: destroying one of the two write-time facts must not launder a procedure into recall. The mutant V-KIND-STAMPED names is 'silently procedural' — treated correctly but NOT counted, which passes every accounting check while erasing the tamper signal. This cell is the one that moves the count.

restore_both_absence_dimensions.derives_from: v12 restore matrix; external round 3 additional correction 3

expect.basis present, NO procedural stamp: MALFORMED, refused per record — the dimension v11's matrix did not cover
expect.consistent record (both present, or neit: restores VERBATIM, the file's own stamp and basis preserved as its history
expect.registry signal: SILENT on restore — the operator is re-asserting this store's past and the registry may have changed since; a registry that shrank must not refuse the store's own records

restore_both_absence_dimensions.setup: `restore=True`, which re-asserts the store's OWN past
restore_both_absence_dimensions.why_it_matters: restore and default import differ in exactly one signal, and stating only the absence dimension v11 covered would have left the other reachable and unspecified.

revoked_source_at_write.derives_from: §4b (v10): record_procedure applies the standing-revocation check exactly as ingest_event does; §8's 'The write surface honours revocation'; V-BIRTH-QUARANTINE-HOLDS
revoked_source_at_write.setup: a procedural write whose source_id digests to a STANDING-REVOKED identity for that user
revoked_source_at_write.then: a LATER revocation of the same source invalidates the record -> withheld:inactive, and the disclosure does NOT change (the sweep never writes disclosure; RECOMPUTED_FIELDS excludes it — the ratchet rule)
revoked_source_at_write.why_it_matters: this is the cell that would fail if the new write surface skipped birth-quarantine — a revocation bypass on the one content type the spec exists to be careful about. It is NOT covered by the resurfacing class (96/96), which predates this surface.

stamp_survives_registry_change.expect: no stored record's list membership or outcome changes — kind is read from the stamp, never from the registry
stamp_survives_registry_change.setup: write records under a registry, then RESHAPE the active registry (reclassify a procedural relation as declarative, and drop another relation entirely); re-read
stamp_survives_registry_change.why_it_matters: this is the whole of V-KIND-STAMPED as an observable. Its mutant (read the registry instead of the stamp) passes the entire 972-cell cross, because every cell is generated under ONE registry. Only a cell that CHANGES the registry between write and read can catch it.

named_cells.withheld_query_blind: the same record under two different queries and the null query must yield byte-identical `withheld` membership AND order

pass_criteria_precommitted: (1) EXACTNESS — every cell's expected list membership and named outcome, 100%
(2) every cell is ALSO absent from both of recall's blocks
(3) the existence-oracle cell is byte-identical, not merely 'empty both times'
(4) `withheld` is query-blind in membership AND order
(5) the accounting identity holds on a population ABOVE the cap, so it cannot pass on a small store

recognition_rule.measured_error_in_the_other_direction: the same rule caught 31.6% of procedural texts (108/342); every miss was structural (quote-stripped spans). NOT this surface's number — its inputs are host-authored summaries, not arbitrary user text.
recognition_rule.must_match: the corpus's frozen procedure texts (openers and step markers DERIVED from them at test time, never hand-listed)

recognition_rule.v1_paraphrase_boundary: exact-form recognition only. A paraphrased summary is a KNOWN PASS (expected DESCRIBED) — the corpus documents the limit rather than pretending it away.

representation_note.do_not_confuse_two_fields: `Provenance.record_kind` (the RECORD's stamp; domain {null, "procedural"}) is NOT `RelationDefinition.relation_kind` (the REGISTRY's declaration; domain {"declarative", "procedural"}, default "declarative"). The registry field legitimately carries the string this corpus must never carry, and conflating the two is how F1 was written.
representation_note.kind_state: A DERIVED column, not an axis: the reviewer's four-state table as data, so the states are checkable per row instead of described in prose. Values: declarative (null ∧ no basis, never a candidate) · procedural ("procedural" ∧ basis) · basis_unknown ("procedural" ∧ no basis) · kind_conflict (null ∧ basis, procedural by floor, counted).
representation_note.record_kind: The declarative value is JSON `null`, NOT the string "declarative". The field is `Optional[Literal["procedural"]] = None` and a wrap-mode model_serializer OMITS the key when None, which is what keeps a declarative record's export bytes identical to the pre-feature oracle.

row_schema_requirement.rule: EVERY corpus row must be constructible through the actual proposed field type: record_kind ∈ {null, "procedural"}, basis ∈ {null, "stated", "observed"}, and kind_state must equal the four-state table's value for that (record_kind, basis) pair.
row_schema_requirement.the_sharpest_form_of_the_defect: The declarative byte-compatibility this corpus exists to protect depends SPECIFICALLY on None, because the wrap serializer pops the key when None. A record carrying the string "declarative" would serialize the key and break V-DECLARATIVE-UNCHANGED -- so the corpus described 486 records that, could they exist, would violate the very invariant it was written to defend.
row_schema_requirement.why_this_exists: External round 3 F1. 486 of 972 cells carried the string "declarative", a value `Optional[Literal["procedural"]]` CANNOT HOLD. It survived two seats, a bidirectional digest binding and a seven-mutation suite because NOTHING EVER CONSTRUCTED A `Provenance` FROM A ROW: the generator guaranteed consistency with the PREDICATE, and every pin test compares digests, data to data. Research had argued a generated corpus "cannot disagree with the predicate it came from" -- true, and silent about the schema, which is exactly where the disagreement was. A digest binding proves two artifacts match; it cannot prove either one is well formed.

spec_pin.anchoring_matters: The anchor at column 0 is doing real work: §6a's own prose mentions `corpus sha256: …` mid-line when describing the binding. An unanchored match would strip prose.
spec_pin.note: The excluded line is what makes the binding non-circular: dev binds the corpus digest into that line AFTER this pin is computed, and the pin is unaffected by design. Any other edit to the spec MOVES this pin and requires a re-pin. Amendment 3: the pin is over v12 and does NOT depend on the corpus digest line, which still held the SUPERSEDED 57668e1f… when this pin was computed — that is the non-circularity working, not an oversight. Dev binds the new digest into that line after this.
spec_pin.reference_impl_python: lines = spec_text.split("\n"); hits = [l for l in lines if l.startswith("corpus sha256: ")]; assert len(hits) == 1; sha256("\n".join(l for l in lines if not l.startswith("corpus sha256: ")).encode())
spec_pin.reference_impl_shell: [ "$(grep -c '^corpus sha256: ' SPEC)" = 1 ] && grep -v '^corpus sha256: ' SPEC | sha256sum
spec_pin.rule: Remove EXACTLY the lines whose text begins with "corpus sha256: " at column 0 (the line and its terminator; nothing else), then sha256 the remaining bytes. There MUST be exactly one such line — assert it and fail otherwise, rather than silently hashing a spec with zero or two.
spec_pin.second_line_hazard_at_acceptance: §6a says that at acceptance the same digest MOVES INTO `## Review closure`. If that lands as a second column-0 "corpus sha256: " line, grep -v removes BOTH while a count=1 regex removes only the FIRST — the two impls would silently diverge exactly at acceptance. The exactly-one assertion above turns that divergence into a test failure instead of a wrong pin.
spec_pin.why_this_rule_and_not_a_regex:
A regex of the form `^corpus sha256: \S+\s*$
?` OVER-DELETES: `\s` matches newline, so `\s*` greedily consumes the blank line that follows §6a's digest line as well. On the v11 working tree it consumed "corpus sha256: CORPUS-DIGEST-NOT-YET-BOUND

" and digested to c18c10c07329807d…, which is NOT the digest of the spec-minus-that-line. §6a says the manifest removes THE LINE; a rule that also removes an adjacent blank line makes the pin sensitive to formatting the spec never claimed was load-bearing.
